description:
## Question

How does each of the six target workloads (see "Choose the target workload set") get into the catalog to the verdict's evidence bar (see "What must docs/verdict.md contain to count as done?"): how the anchor package's Elixir version and NIF are brought in (Mix.install of the package, vendored copy, or a faithful port), how responsiveness (worst tick gap) is measured beside the NIF, how small/large sizes and the crossover are reported, and which build tickets are handed off to the catalog epic (defk-9p6) with which real technical blockers (bitwise ops, [f32], [i16]/[i32], wrapping arithmetic, bit output).

comments.text: Per 'State kept between kernel calls' (defk-dtw.9): confirm that ex_data_sketch's Rust NIF also copies the HLL register binary per call (expected, since BEAM binaries are immutable), so the small-size comparison is like for like.

Per 'What do narrow element types ([f32], [i16], [i32]) mean in a kernel?' (defk-dtw.13): the [f32] and [i16]/[i32] blocker is now the build ticket 'Add [i16], [i32] and [f32] element types' (defk-4ai).

Per 'Can a kernel produce variable-length bit output, and in what form?' (defk-dtw.14): Gorilla's bit-output blocker is [Add the bitstring accumulator](defk-cmr); its bit reinterpretation is Defk.Bits.f64_to_u64/1, to be built with the rest of Defk.Bits and u64 from defk-dtw.10 (no build ticket for those exists yet; hand it off here).

title: Plan the catalog build for the six target workloads
